needs_login: This device needs to be logged in to Tailscale. Refresh this page after logging in to see the status, bestie.
tailscale_disabled: Tailscale is currently off. You can switch it on in the Settings tab, no cap.

settings.unraid_listen: Unraid services listen on Tailscale IP, no cap
settings.tpm: Allow TPM to Encrypt Node Key

context.tpm: Enables use of a TPM (Trusted Platform Module) for secure storage of the Tailscale node key. This boosts security by making the node key harder to extract, so only authorized hardware can access it. This requires TPM 2.0. It does nothing if the system does not have a compatible TPM.
context.unraid_listen: Sets up Unraid services (SSH, WebGUI, SMB, etc.) to listen on Tailscale addresses.
context.ip_forward: Sets net.ipv4.ip_forward and net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding to 1 in sysctl. This hits instantly when you enable it.
context.taildrop: Pick the path for incoming Taildrop files.
context.dns: Lets Tailscale DNS be enabled via the CLI or WebGUI. If off, Tailscale DNS will stay off when Tailscale starts.
context.subnets: Lets Tailscale routes be enabled via the CLI or WebGUI. If off, Tailscale routes will stay off when Tailscale starts.
context.wireguard: Change the port used for Wireguard connections. Usually you do not need to touch this, fr.
context.erase: Logs out of Tailscale and resets all settings to default vibes
context.restart: Restart the Tailscale daemon and reapply settings, easy clap.
context.diagnostics: Download diagnostics (this might take a hot sec)
context.save: Tailscale will restart when changes are applied
context.reauthenticate: Force a Tailscale reauthentication, no cap.
context.funnel: Lets Tailscale funnel be enabled via the WebGUI. If off, Tailscale funnel will be disabled.
context.hosts: Adds Tailscale peers to /etc/hosts for name resolution. Useful if you want to use Tailnet DNS names without the possible chaos of enabling Tailscale DNS on the server.
context.no_logs_no_support: Turns off Tailscale telemetry and opts you out of getting support from Tailscale when that telemetry would be needed for debugging.

info.exit_node_local: Allow LAN Access while using Exit Node
info.unapproved: Needs approval in admin console, chief

warnings.key_expiration: The Tailscale key expires in %s days on %s, heads up.
warnings.netbios: NetBIOS is enabled in SMB settings — this can block shares from being accessed via Tailscale.
warnings.lock: The tailnet has lock on, but this node is unsigned. It will not be able to talk to the tailnet.
warnings.funnel: Enabling Tailscale Funnel for the Unraid WebGUI exposes your server to the internet, which seriously boosts the risk of unauthorized access and potential attacks. Only turn this on if you fully get the security impact. The recommended secure play for remote access is to install Tailscale on the devices you plan to use to access the WebGUI instead of enabling Funnel.
warnings.subnet: Accepting Tailscale subnets on your Unraid server can mess with local network connectivity in some setups. Accepting routes is not required for your Unraid server to work as a subnet router or exit node. Only enable this if your Unraid server needs to connect to remote subnets advertised by other devices.
warnings.dns: Enabling Tailscale MagicDNS on your server can mess with name resolution inside Docker containers, potentially causing app connectivity issues. MagicDNS does not need to be enabled on the server for you to access your Unraid server using MagicDNS names (e.g., 'unraid.tailnet.ts.net') from other devices. Enabling 'Add Peers to /etc/hosts' is the safer play and lets Tailscale names be used on the server.
warnings.caution: Proceed carefully and make sure you understand what this change does before continuing.
warnings.peer_relay_no_acl: Not configured in Tailnet policy (access controls), kinda sus.
warnings.tpm: Enabling the TPM locks the Tailscale node key to this device's specific hardware. If the TPM is later disabled, the Tailscale node key becomes invalid and the device will need to reauthenticate to Tailscale. TPMs can also lock out, which can mess up Tailscale connectivity and require reauthentication.
